senses.class: verb root (own entry SK-at-p18-0220 'at' VI (1) 'go; walk'; Grammatical Overview: 'the root at to go')
senses.evidence: Own entry SK-at-p18-0220 'go; walk'. Etymologies: SK-kaaqat-p2-0010 <kaa+at, go inside>; SK-huukat-p398-3872 <huuk+at, go inside>; SK-wicat-p178-3529 <wic+at, go to a point>. Every one of the 178 uses is translated 'go' (or a motion reading built on it: ra.at 'go carrying = take', u.at 'go/extend in a line').
senses.doubts: None about the meaning. Parks's own entry lists suppletive partner stems (du. war, dist. warii, pl./impf. wuu, int. huhta); these are separate stems, not shapes of at.

forms.notes: Counted: entries whose printed etymology has 'at' as an exact piece (split on +, . and spaces; bound/line-break hyphens stripped; preverb notes such as (ut...) ignored) = 178. The same counting method is used for every form in this file. Usually stem-final; common fixed combinations are ra.at 'take, carry', u.at 'go in a line', wic+at 'arrive (going)'.

senses.class: verb root (own entry SK-raquk-p114-2221 'raʔuk' VT (3) 'make; construct, build; give birth to; paint')
senses.evidence: Own entry SK-raquk-p114-2221. Etymologies with a noun object: SK-akaraquk-p11-0110 <akaar+raʔuk, make a dwelling>; SK-huuraquk-p51-0853 huu+raʔuk, make mush; SK-ituraquk-p418-3917 itur+raʔuk, make a village.

shapes.evidence: Own entry gives 'pl. obj. karaʔuk'; SK-karaquk-p77-1406 <ka+raʔuk, ITER + make>. A derived stem (ka- + raʔuk), not a variant shape.

senses.doubts: The line between 'make N' and the causative sense below is mine: I put here the 37 etymologies whose literal translation is 'make' + a noun (or bare 'make'), including four 'pick/pluck/extract' verbs that Parks explains as 'make' (SK-taraquk-p159-3108 ta+raʔuk, make, i.e., pluck, suspended; also 3177, 3444, 0918). A few are borderline (e.g. SK-raaqiitustarahkistaquk-p115-2240 'make a strong word', SK-iciiraraquk-p56-0964 'make mischief').

senses.meaning: cause to be, make (into a state): causative of descriptive and other stems
senses.label: CAUS
senses.evidence: abbreviations.json: CAUS 'causative' lists '-ik, -k, raʔuk, -wuh'; Grammatical Overview Table 15, slot 8 Causative '-rik-, -raʔuk'. Etymologies: SK-tarahkistaquk-p160-3136 <tarahkiis+raʔuk, cause to be strong>; SK-ahihaquk-p9-0091 ahiht+raʔuk, cause to be fat; SK-iiraquk-p408-3909 ii+raʔuk, ii + cause. Parks alternates 'cause to be X' and 'make X' freely (SK-kasistaquk-p79-1463 <kasis+raʔuk, make hard>).

shapes.evidence: Three further etymologies print the piece broken by a line-end hyphen: SK-ikiriwiihaquk-p62-1064 <ikiriwit+ra-ʔuk, cause to be changed>, SK-kicapictaquk-p85-1590, SK-kiiskawaarasihaquk-p92-1736 (checked on PDF page 92: line break). Not included in n_words.

senses.doubts: Almost certainly the same morpheme as the verb 'make' used as a causative; I separate the two only because Parks lists raʔuk both as a verb headword and under CAUS.

forms.notes: 124 exact-piece etymologies (37 + 87). Not counted: 3 with the line-break spelling ra-ʔuk and SK-ckahiikaraquks-p30-0462 (hiika-raʔuk.his). Always the last element of the stem; surface forms -taʔuk / -haʔuk / -raʔuk follow regular sound changes.

senses.meaning: way, custom, tradition; activity, event; matter; time
senses.class: noun root (dependent noun: own entry SK-raa--p114-2225 'raa-' N-DEP 'way, custom, tradition; activity, event; time'; independent noun SK-raaquq-p115-2248 raaʔuʔ; also SK-raa-p114-2224 'raa' VD 'be a way, matter; be a custom')
senses.evidence: SK-raaquq-p115-2248 raa+uʔ, way + NOM; SK-raahiir-p117-2271 <raa+hiir (uur...), be a nice way>; SK-raaqaawaa-p114-2226 raa+aawaa, leave a way. Nearly all literal translations say 'way'; 'time' in SK-raawiikatk-p127-2498 raa.awi+ukatk, cut time.
senses.doubts: Includes a handful where Parks's literal translation does not say 'way' but the compound is built on a raa- stem he glosses that way elsewhere (e.g. SK-raaqiitusuq-p115-2242 raa.iitus+uʔ, be a story + NOM; SK-raasaar-p124-2431 <raa+asaar, be the name of an object>; SK-raaripakusuq-p123-2402).

senses.label: PL
senses.evidence: SK-raakii-p119-2322 <raa+kii, PL + to be strung>; SK-raakirikaaqat-p119-2331 <raa+kirik.kaaʔat, eye to go inside + PL>; SK-raaqat-p114-2228 ut+raa+at, go for things. Also 'things/everything' in 2441, 2330, 2332.

examples.raw_etymology: <raa+kii+raʔuk, cause PL to be strung in a line>

senses.doubts: Parks prints the label PL for raa in only three etymologies (2322, 2325, 2331); the other four say 'things'/'everything'. This may simply be the noun raa- 'way, matter' used generically ('things'), or a variant of the plural prefix raar-; the sources do not decide. Treat as doubtful.

senses.class: noun root (kin term stem: own entry SK--raa-p114-2223 '-raa' N-KIN)
senses.evidence: Own entry SK--raa-p114-2223 '-raa' N-KIN 'mother (only with 1st person possessor)'; SK-atiraq-p19-0243 ati+raa, my mother.

forms.notes: 166 exact-piece etymologies. Unassigned (6): SK-wakta/taa-p175-3476 <wak+raa, sound + raa> (Parks leaves raa unglossed); SK-aar_iraariq-p351-3600 <ar i+raa+riʔ, be friends + his/her same-sex sibling> (the kin stem is raar per SK-iraariq-p64-1121 <i+raar+riʔ>, so not this raa); SK-raawaasit-p126-2461 <raa.waa.asit, be cold + DIST>; SK-raawacuuquq-p126-2465 <raa.wacuu+uʔ, quiver + NOM>; SK-raawiiraarik-p127-2500 and SK-raawiirakus-p127-2501 (raa.awiira 'crowd'). Two further headwords have the same shape but do not occur as etymology pieces: SK-ra,_raa-p114-2216 'ra, raa' CONJ 'now; and' and SK-raa--p114-2222 'raa-' ADV-P 'just'. So raa is at least a three-way homonym (way / mother / conjunction-adverb), plus the doubtful PL use.

senses.meaning: be sitting, be seated; (of things) be situated, be in a place
senses.class: verb root (positional verb: own entry SK-kus-p102-1993 'kus' VI (4) 'be sitting, be seated; be, be living (in a place); live')
senses.evidence: Own entry SK-kus-p102-1993 (pl. subj. wihak). Etymologies: SK-kaakus-p72-1294 <kaa+kus, be sitting inside an enclosed space >; SK-kuusk-p452-4010 <kus+k, cause to be sitting>; SK-kitakus-p98-1912 kita+kus, be sitting on top.

examples.raw_etymology: <kaa+kus, be sitting inside an enclosed space >

senses.doubts: None. With inanimate subjects the translation is often just 'be' (a village, a pool, a clump) but Parks still renders it 'to be sitting'.

forms.notes: 102 exact-piece etymologies, all 'sit'. Hyphenated extras not counted: SK-ihtatakuusk-p59-1036 (ihtata-kus+k) and SK-awirahkirikus-p25-0333 (kiri-kus) are the same verb; pit-kus (SK-pitkusuusiriq-p114-2213, 'two') and ic-kus (SK-siraackuskasara-p152-2977, ickus 'tail end') are not.

senses.class: verb root (own entry SK-a-p349-3577 'a' VI (3) (ir...) 'come'; takes the preverb ir-)
senses.evidence: Own entry SK-a-p349-3577; Grammatical Overview: stem 'a (ir-...) to come'. Etymologies: SK-raqa-p114-2217 ra+a (ir...), come carrying; SK-wica-p178-3526 <wic+a (ir...), come to a point>; SK-huuka-p49-0839 huuk+a (ir...), come inside.
senses.doubts: Stem-final, nearly always with the note (ir...). Paired with at 'go' (kaaʔa 'come inside' / kaaʔat 'go inside').

senses.meaning: extending in a line (distributive counterpart of u-)
senses.class: locative (own entry SK-a--p349-3576 'a-' LOC 'extending in a line'; SK-u--p167-3294 'u-' LOC gives 'dist. a-')
senses.evidence: SK-ahak-p9-0087 a+hak, pass in a line; SK-awarik-p21-0273 <a-+warik, cause to go in a line>; SK-awarii-p21-0272 <a+warii, go around in a line>.

examples.raw_etymology: <a-+warik, cause to go in a line>
<a- +wuu, be going in a line, i.e., flying>
iks+a.wuu, hand to be going in a line

shapes.evidence: SK-u--p167-3294 'u-' LOC 'extending in a line' lists a- as its distributive form (uhak / ahak 'extend in a line'). Paradigm partner rather than the same shape.

senses.doubts: A few are assigned by analogy with awarik/awaahak rather than by an explicit 'in a line' in the translation (SK-katiitawaa-p83-1536 <katiit+a.waa, black(ness) spreads out >, SK-kiicawarik-p89-1658, SK-uhuriiwaawarik-p169-3335).

senses.meaning: be stretched out (as a staked hide)
senses.class: locative (locative-class verb: own entry SK-a-p349-3575 'a' VL 'be stretched out, as a staked hide being tanned')
senses.evidence: Own entry SK-a-p349-3575; SK-awuh-p26-0353 <a- +wuh, cause to be stretched out >.
senses.doubts: Probably the same element as a- 'extending in a line'; kept apart because Parks has separate headwords.

senses.meaning: be an image, picture, design (of someone/something); be decorated
senses.class: other (locative-class verb with preverb: own entry SK-a-p349-3579 'a' VL (uur...) 'be decorated; have a picture or design; be a photograph')
senses.evidence: SK-a-p349-3579 <a (uur...), be one's image>; SK-awuh-p26-0354 <a (uur...)+wuh, cause to be an image>; SK-kaahuraara-p72-1278 <kaahuraar+a (uur...), be a picture of the world>.

examples.raw_etymology: <kaahuraar+a (uur...), be a picture of the world>
<ra+aak+a.waa.wuh (uur...)+hus, one that/who makes pictures of them >
<hiwat+a, be a doorway image; i.q. SB hiwata; cf. Ar. huwaat, huuwaat be an entryway>

senses.doubts: SK-hiwata-p43-0711 <hiwat+a, be a doorway image; ...> has no (uur...) note. Two similar 'be X' formations I left unassigned: SK-kica-p84-1569 <kic+a, be liquid> and SK-uukaqaata,_uukaata-p172-3396 <uukaʔaat+a, be a shadow; ...>.

senses.meaning: your (second person possessor on kin terms)
senses.label: 2.POSS
senses.evidence: SK-akaq-p9-0103 a+kaa, your grandmother; SK-aqas-p349-3581 <a+as, your father>; SK-asas-p363-3759 a+saas, your mother. abbreviations.json has 2.POSS 'second person possessive prefix' (no form printed) and 2.P 'second person patientive prefix' a-.
senses.doubts: The label 2.POSS is my choice from the abbreviation list; the etymologies only translate it 'your'. Occurs only on kinship terms.

senses.class: other (conjunction: own entry SK-a,_aa-p349-3580 'a, aa' CONJ 'and')
senses.evidence: Own entry SK-a,_aa-p349-3580; SK-aki-p11-0117 <a+ki, and + here>; SK-aku-p11-0127 <a+ku, and perhaps>.

shapes.evidence: Headword 'a, aa' CONJ (SK-a,_aa-p349-3580).

Optional 'and' in numerals, not counted in n_words: SK-kskiitikstaaruq-ruksiriq,_kski-p101-1942 <kskiitiks(.raaruʔ).(a.)ruksiriʔ, eighty (and) ten>; also SK-pitkusuraaruq-ruksiriq,_pitkus-p114-2212 and SK-tawiraaruq-ruksiriq,_tawiraaru-p164-3222.

senses.class: other (verb inflected like a locative verb, VT (wi), with preverbs ir...ut...)
senses.evidence: SK-iksa-p62-1076 <iks+a (ir...ut...), wear on the hand>; SK-kiica-p89-1655 <kiic+a (ir...ut...), wear on the neck>; SK-iksawuh-p63-1083 ut-+iks+a.wuh, cause to wear on one's wrist.

examples.raw_etymology: <haas+kiic.a (ir ...ut...), wear a string around the neck>
kiiriit.arik+a (ir...ut...), wear a horn, i.e., queue, on the nape
ut-+iks+a.wuh, cause to wear on one's wrist

senses.doubts: No headword of its own. Could be a use of the locative verb a ('be stretched out / be on') rather than a separate root; the sources do not say.

senses.class: verb root (own entry SK-aa/a-p349-3587 'aa/a' VT (4) 'eat'; dist. waawaa, waʔaa)
senses.evidence: Own entry SK-aa/a-p349-3587; SK-riiripiipahu-p141-2814 <ra+ir+ripiik-+wa.a.hus, eating eggs>; SK-raawisaa/a-p128-2518 raawis+aa/a, eat smoke (piece printed 'aa/a').

shapes.evidence: Headword 'aa/a' (SK-aa/a-p349-3587); the piece is printed aa/a in SK-raawisaa/a-p128-2518, which is not included in n_words.

senses.doubts: Basic shape is aa; short a only by rule. Only one etymology has the bare piece 'a' in this meaning.

senses.label: SUB.1
senses.evidence: abbreviations.json: verb class (1) '-a suffixed to dependent forms', (1-a) '-a, -asta', SUB.1 'subordinating suffix of Class 1 verbs'. Etymologies: SK-tiirukcaakata-p165-3255 <tii+ra+uks+saak+at+a, this day that went>; SK-ruuhtahariwaara-p149-2900 <ra+taha+hiir (uur...)+waa+a, ones that taste good + DIST>.

examples.raw_etymology: tii+hii+ra+uks+saak+at+a, this other day that went

senses.doubts: Parks does not label this piece in the etymologies; the identification rests on its position after class 1 stems (at, hiir) in nominalised forms and on the abbreviation list. SK-piitahaawiraata-p113-2178 <wiita+haawiraat.a, man going downstream> is the least certain.

forms.notes: 142 raw exact-piece hits; 7 are not uses of a morpheme and were dropped (English article 'a' inside cf.-notes: SK-aahka-p349-3590, SK-haahka-p33-0550, SK-hukaa-p43-0724, SK-iciis-p56-0966, SK-kuuskahaar-p452-4011, SK-rikiis-p492-4174; letter-spaced print in SK-ø_(ut...)_kiirahkata-p349-3572). That leaves 135 entries; SK-awica-p370-3780 <a.wic+a (ir...)> and SK-awaqa-p20-0251 a+wa.a (ir...) contain both 'in a line' and 'come' and are counted in both senses. Unassigned (4): SK-kica-p84-1569 and SK-uukaqaata,_uukaata-p172-3396 ('be X'), SK-awatata--p21-0277 <ut+awatat.a, on top of, covering> and SK-haakaawatataquq-p33-0561 (awatat.a). In SK-rahiisa-p478-4124 <ra+a+hiis+a, the coming morning> the last a is 'come' (counted) and the first is probably the third-person preverb a- (PREV.3.A in abbreviations.json), not counted. Hyphenated strings such as a-rii, a-paak, a-wis are line-break spellings of longer pieces. A learner should treat 'a' as at least five unrelated items: come, in-a-line, your, and, eat.

senses.class: noun root (dependent noun: own entry SK-aciks--p352-3615 'aciks-' N-DEP 'spirit, mind, thoughts, feelings, emotions; throat'; also SK-aciks-p352-3614 'aciks' VD 'have a thought')
senses.evidence: SK-ciksuq-p29-0448 <aciks+uʔ, mind + NOM>; SK-aciksiir-p352-3628 <aciks-+hiir (uur...), mind to be good>; SK-acikstarahkiis/kis-p7-0055 aciks+tarahkiis, mind to be strong.

shapes.evidence: Own entry gives the combining form '(a)ciks-'; printed so in SK-aar_ciksuq-p351-3599 <aar (ut...) (a)ciks+uʔ, do thoughts>, SK-aar_ciksuq-p351-3597 and SK-ø_(ut...)_ciksuq-p349-3571 (3 more entries, not in n_words). The initial a also drops in independent words: ciksuʔ, cikstit.

senses.doubts: Parks translates the piece as 'mind', 'thoughts' or 'feelings' without a consistent difference.

senses.class: noun root (second gloss 'throat' of the same headword SK-aciks--p352-3615, whose printed etymology is <aciks, throat>)
senses.evidence: SK-acikcak-p351-3613 <aciks+cak, strike the trachea>; SK-acikstaahiis-p7-0051 aciks+taahiis, trachea to be dry; SK-cikstiituq-p29-0446 <aciks-+tiit+uʔ, eye of the trachea + NOM>.

examples.raw_etymology: aciks+riiwaktaa, emit a groaning sound in the trachea

senses.doubts: Not a homonym in Parks's treatment: one headword with two glosses (the throat as seat of thought and feeling; ciksuʔ means both 'esophagus, trachea' and 'mind'). Two entries carry both readings and are counted under 'mind': SK-acikskiwatak-p354-3653 <aciks+kiwatak, mind/windpipe to fade> and SK-ciksuq-p29-0448.

forms.notes: 88 exact-piece etymologies (82 + 6), nearly always stem-initial.

senses.class: noun root (independent noun kiicuʔ 'water; liquid'; Parks's own headword is the descriptive verb SK-kic-p84-1568 'kic' VD 'be a liquid; be watery')
senses.evidence: SK-kiicuq-p89-1678 <kic+uʔ, water + NOM>; SK-kickus-p87-1640 kic+kus, water to be sitting; SK-iitkiicuq-p61-1050 <iit+kic+uʔ, breast liquid + NOM>.
senses.doubts: Parks alternates 'water' and 'liquid' with no difference. A second stem kiir is also translated 'water' (SK-kiiraquk-p90-1699 <kiir+raʔuk, make water>); I cannot tell from the sources whether it is related.

forms.notes: 119 exact-piece etymologies. Unassigned: SK-uukickata--p172-3406 <uu.kata+kic, on the west side + kic> (Parks leaves kic unglossed). Not counted: SK-kickaqaahis-p86-1603 'shoulder' (kic-ka.aahis, opaque).

senses.meaning: suspended, hanging; hang (be on, as from a line); with motion verbs 'up'
senses.class: locative (own entries SK-ta--p153-2992 'ta-' LOC 'suspended, hanging, dangling' and SK-ta-p153-2991 'ta' VL 'hang suspended; be suspended, pendent')
senses.evidence: SK-tawuh-p164-3228 ta+wuh, cause to be suspended; SK-awita-p25-0345 <awi+ta, image to be suspended>; SK-taqat-p153-2994 ta+at, go suspended. 'Up' readings: SK-saaktaqa-p151-2939 <saak+ta.a (ir...), sun to come suspended>.
senses.doubts: Includes ta.wi 'be suspended upright' = slope, incline (SK-tawi-p163-3196) and derived verbs where the translation is only 'over' or 'on' (SK-hactawiqat-p37-0631 <hat+ta.wi.at, rub the tongue over>; SK-hiihtakus-p389-3822 <hiir-+ta+kus, grass to be sitting on>, which could equally be the general locative below).

senses.label: GEN.LOC
senses.evidence: SK-takaas-p157-3063 ta+kaas, GEN.LOC + crack; SK-taraasit-p159-3114 ta+raasit, GEN.LOC + be frozen; SK-racakus-p129-2541 <raar-+ta+kus, PL + GEN.LOC + be sitting>. abbreviations.json: GEN.LOC 'general locative prefix'.

examples.raw_etymology: <ta+watur, GEN.LOC + between; cf. Ar. tawatur be an open space>

shapes.evidence: abbreviations.json prints the form of GEN.LOC as taa-; in the dictionary etymologies the piece labelled GEN.LOC is always ta. I found no etymology piece taa with this label.

senses.doubts: Whether this is a different morpheme from 'suspended' is unclear; SK-taruuc-p161-3165 <ta+ruuc, GEN.LOC + PL to be lying sus-pended> mixes the two. 18 entries carry the printed label; SK-kiictawakuq-p89-1673 (ta.wakaʔu) is added because tawakaʔu is labelled so in SK-tawakaqu-p162-3182.

forms.notes: 103 exact-piece etymologies. Unassigned (7), all with ta unglossed: SK-tararit-p160-3142 <ta+rarit, cf. rarit be lit, as a fire> and the toaster word SK-raracarariiruku_icataaquq-p136-2681; SK-rikiistakakaqus-p492-4190 (ta.ka.kaʔus); SK-racapirat-p129-2547 (ta.pira.at); and three with ta+uukuk 'touch': SK-ikstaquukuk-p63-1098, SK-ritaquukuk-p494-4208, SK-raakstacuukuku_ruurariiruku-p120-2339. The first two are probably GEN.LOC. 26 hyphenated strings (ka-ta = kata, ta-wihk 'three', ta-ha 'flavor', ta-hik 'hit' etc.) are line-break spellings of longer pieces and are not counted.

senses.meaning: image, picture; fleeting image, hence quick motion ('quickly')
senses.class: noun root (dependent noun: own entry SK-awi--p21-0281 'awi-' N-DEP 'fleeting image; quick motion', etymology <awi, image>; Grammatical Overview Table 15, slot 2 Noun: awi- 'image')
senses.evidence: SK-awiquq-p21-0290 <awi+uʔ, image + NOM>; SK-awiqat-p21-0283 <awi+at, image to go, i.e., go quickly>; SK-awiraquk-p24-0326 awi+raʔuk, make an image.

examples.raw_etymology: <awi+at, image to go, i.e., go quickly>
awi+kusik, image to pick up, i.e., pick up quickly

shapes.evidence: Own entry gives the combining forms 'awi-, aʔi-'; printed in SK-aqiwaahcik-p349-3583 <aʔi-waahc+ik, cause to separate>. Surface aʔi- before w (aʔiwarik from awi.warik).

senses.doubts: One morpheme with two uses that Parks links himself: literal 'image/picture' (71 of the translations use those words) and an adverb-like 'quickly' (32 say quick/fleeting/fast, usually as 'image to X, i.e., X quickly'). About 30 translations mention neither (e.g. awi.warik 'cause to shake', raa.awi 'time', awi+hiir 'nice'); I count them here because the stems are built on awi, but the meaning contribution is not shown.

forms.notes: 108 exact-piece etymologies. Unassigned: SK-picuuwihiriq-p111-2164 <prob. pic+huu.awi+hiriʔ, surface of the heart + LOC; ...> (Parks's own 'prob.').

senses.meaning: against (a vertical surface); up an incline, on an incline
senses.class: locative (own entry SK-kata--p79-1464 'kata-' LOC 'against (a vertical surface); up an incline, on an incline, as steps, a bank, or a hill')
senses.evidence: SK-kataqat-p80-1467 kata+at, go against a vertical surface; SK-katakus-p81-1493 <kata+kus, be sitting against a vertical surface>; SK-katasa-p82-1509 <kata+sa, be lying against a vertical surface>.

examples.raw_etymology: kata+at, go against a vertical surface
<kata+kus, be sitting against a vertical surface>
<kata+sa, be lying against a vertical surface>
kata+iir, put against a vertical surface
kata-+uukuk, bump against a vertical surface

shapes.evidence: Eight further etymologies print the piece with a line-break hyphen, e.g. SK-kataqa-p80-1466 ut+ka-ta+a (ir...), TRANS + come against a vertical surface; SK-rikatahak-p491-4159 ri+ka-ta+hak, take from a vertical surface. Not included in n_words.
SK-huukata(wi)--p398-3873 <huu.kata(.wi), against the surface of water>.

senses.doubts: None on the meaning; extended to 'up the throat' (vomiting, swallowing) and 'on a surface' (spots, patches).

forms.notes: 78 exact-piece etymologies; 9 more with the hyphenated or parenthesised spellings above.

senses.meaning: in, on (a circumscribed space; a bounded horizontal surface)
senses.class: locative (own entry SK-ka--p418-3925 'ka-' LOC 'on a horizontal (bounded) surface'; Grammatical Overview Table 15, slot 5 Locative: ka- 'on')
senses.evidence: SK-kakus-p77-1397 <ka+kus, be sitting in a circumscribed space>; SK-kawarik-p83-1551 <ka+warik, cause to go in/on>; SK-kaquuc/uc--p418-3940 ka+uuc, lay in a circumscribed space.

examples.raw_etymology: <ka+kus, be sitting in a circumscribed space>
ka+uuc, lay in a circumscribed space

senses.doubts: Parks's literal translations mostly say only 'in/on'. Several verbs here are glossed for both this sense and the 'brush' sense (kakus, kasa, kaarik, kawiitik, kaʔat, kaʔiir, kaʔuuc, kawiʔat). SK-karuuc-p79-1452 <ka+ruuc, ITER + be lying in/on> is ambiguous between this and ITER.

senses.class: locative (own entry SK-ka--p418-3924 'ka-' LOC 'in brush, grass, timber, woods')

senses.meaning: iterative: repeated action, or action on plural objects
senses.label: ITER
senses.evidence: abbreviations.json: ITER 'iterative prefix' ka-, raar-/rah-; Grammatical Overview Table 15, slot 1 Iterative 'raar-, ka- ITER'. Etymologies: SK-kacak-p75-1352 ka+cak, ITER + strike; SK-karaquk-p77-1406 <ka+raʔuk, ITER + make>; SK-kapic/piqic-p77-1402 <ka+apic, ITER + break>.
senses.doubts: Stands directly before the verb root (often after an incorporated noun: huraar+ka.raʔuk). 14 of the 30 are compounds built on karaʔuk 'make (pl. obj.)' where Parks does not always repeat the label (e.g. SK-icakaraquk-p54-0918 'extract/pull PL from the end').

senses.meaning: way, manner of acting or doing; act, behavior, movement (Parks often translates it 'image')
senses.class: noun root (independent noun SK-uhuuruq-p170-3353 uhuuruʔ 'way, manner of acting or of doing something'; also SK-uhuur_[+_raar-]-p169-3342 VD 'be thus, be a certain way')

shapes.evidence: SK-uhuuwaturikat-p170-3355 uhuu(r)+waturika+t, image between + LOC.

Possibly a short form: translated 'image' in SK-huhtaat/taqat-p43-0719 <huur-+ta.at, image goes suspended> and SK-huuricka--p51-0862 huur+icka, image face (compare SK-uhuurickat-p169-3349). Most other huur pieces mean 'have the quality of / place', so this is uncertain.

senses.doubts: The English glosses vary (image, way, act, behavior/activity/action, movement); Parks joins them himself ('image/way', 'image/act'), so I keep one sense. 'Image' here is not a picture but a moving figure, as with awi.

senses.label: SUB.D
senses.evidence: abbreviations.json: SUB.D 'descriptive stem subordinating suffix' -u; Grammatical Overview: 'Descriptive stems ... take the subordinate suffix -u'. Etymologies: SK-rahaaktaakaaru-p478-4119 <ra+haak+taakaar+u, wood that is white>; SK-rakaahuraahkatiitu-p134-2610 <ra+kaahuraar+katiit+u, the world that is black>; SK-piitaraqu-p113-2181 <piita+ra.u, being the man>.
senses.doubts: Parks never labels this piece in the etymologies; the identification is from its position after descriptive stems in ra- nominalisations (13 entries) and from the abbreviation list. Nine entries are less direct: the kin expressions with ra.u 'being' (0266, 0409, 0539, 1977, 2181) and haa.u 'have as a child' (1973, 1974, 1978, 1979).

senses.meaning: stem-forming suffix on descriptive bases ('activizer'; once 'transitivizer')
senses.label: ACT
senses.evidence: SK-ickaqu-p57-0974 <icka+u, sharp + ACT>; SK-hiikaqu-p389-3825 <hiika (uur...)+u, clean + ACT>; SK-wakaqu-p175-3464 <waka+u, (to) voice + TRANS>. abbreviations.json: ACT 'activizer suffix' -aʔu, -a, -uk; TRANS 'transitivizer affix' includes -u.
senses.doubts: Label printed in four of the six (ACT in 0974, 3825, 1570; TRANS in 3464); SK-iciiraqu-p56-0963 <iciira+u, be mischievous; ...> and SK-kirikaqu-p96-1827 <kirika+u, be awake> are assigned by parallel shape. Whether ACT -u and TRANS -u are one suffix is not shown.

forms.notes: 64 raw exact-piece hits; 2 dropped (letter-spaced '( u t . . . )' in SK-ø_(ut...)_kiirahkata-p349-3572 and SK-ø_(ut...)_pak_siriq-p349-3573). Unassigned: SK-kitkahaahkisuraariksisuq-p99-1925 kitkahaahkis.u+raariksis+uʔ, real Kitkahahki + NOM. Not counted: u(k) 'legging?' in SK-ukuuk-p171-3381 and SK-ukuukuquq-p171-3383, and line-break strings u-huur, u-kac. Note the NOM suffix is uʔ, a different piece. So 'u' is one lexical locative plus two unrelated grammatical suffixes.

senses.meaning: be big, large; (of rain, wind, sound) heavy, strong, loud
senses.class: descriptive stem (own entry SK-rihuur-p139-2764 'rihuur' VD 'be big, large; be noted, prominent, socially important')
senses.evidence: Own entry SK-rihuur-p139-2764. Etymologies: SK-iturihuur-p418-3919 itur+rihuur, be a big village; SK-haakarihuur-p34-0576 <haaka+rihuur, mouth to be large>; SK-rihuraar-p139-2763 <rihuur+aar, become big>.

shapes.evidence: Line-break spelling in SK-awirihuur-p25-0337 <awi+ri-huur, be a big image>; not in n_words.

senses.doubts: None; every etymology says 'big' or 'large'.

forms.notes: 21 exact-piece etymologies. Normally stem-final after a noun; surface -tihuur/-hihuur after some consonants.

senses.meaning: wood; tree; a piece of wood (stick, pole, pipestem)
senses.class: noun root (dependent noun: own entry SK-haak-,_rak--p33-0557 'haak-, rak-' N-DEP 'wood; tree'; also SK-haak/haaqak-p33-0558 VL 'be a tree; be wood, a pole, post, stick')
senses.evidence: SK-haaktaquk-p35-0594 haak+raʔuk, make a (piece of) wood; SK-haakahuruus-p33-0564 <haak+kahuruus, be hollow or pithy wood >; SK-sahtaakuq-p151-2942 <saht+haak+uʔ, walnut wood + NOM; cf. sat walnut>.

examples.raw_etymology: <saht+haak+uʔ, walnut wood + NOM; cf. sat walnut>
haak+wuh, put (a piece of) wood upright

shapes.evidence: Same headword 'haak-, rak-' (SK-haak-,_rak--p33-0557); rak is the piece in 42 further etymologies meaning 'wood', e.g. SK-rakis-p135-2644 <rak+kis, wood + DIM>, SK-rakaatiit-p134-2613 <rak+kaatiit, black wood>. (rak also occurs as an unrelated 'grandchild' stem in SK-arakis-p13-0132 and SK-raktiiki-p135-2664.)
SK-raakickuusuq-p119-2321 <raak+ickuus+uʔ, tree peeling + NOM>; SK-kiriktaakuq-p96-1847 <kirik+raak+uʔ, eye wood + NOM, ...>; SK-raakuq-p120-2340 <raak+uʔ, wood + NOM> 'box'.

senses.doubts: None for haak. How haak-, rak- and raak are distributed is not explained in the sources I used.

forms.notes: 31 exact-piece etymologies, all 'wood/tree' (the 'pipe' readings are 'stick'). Do not confuse with haaka 'mouth'.

senses.class: locative (own entry SK-ha-,_haa--p32-0541 'ha-, haa-' LOC 'in water')
senses.evidence: SK-hakus-p37-0632 <ha+kus, be sitting in water>; SK-hasa-p37-0646 <ha+sa, be lying in water>; SK-haqiir-p32-0542 ha+iir, put in water.

shapes.evidence: Headword 'ha-, haa-'; five etymologies use haa for 'in water', e.g. SK-haaqat-p33-0548 <haa-+at, go in water>, SK-huukitahaawarii-p398-3883 <huukita+haa+warii, go about on top of water>. (Other haa pieces are unrelated: 'child' in SK-haaraquk-p35-0605, LOC.ADV in SK-tiihaataku-p164-3234.)

senses.doubts: ha.wi 'along on water' gives hawi- 'downstream; east' (SK-hawi--p40-0679).

forms.notes: 27 exact-piece etymologies. Unassigned: SK-hawat-p387-3818 <ha+wat, extract from in the mouth; ...> 'spit out', where Parks translates ha as 'in the mouth' (a different element, or an extension I cannot confirm).

senses.class: noun root (independent noun SK-ckaquq-p30-0460 ckaʔuʔ 'face; cloud'; no separate headword for icka-)
senses.evidence: SK-ckaquq-p30-0460 icka+uʔ, face + NOM; SK-ickakaa-p57-0978 <icka+kaa, face to be inside>; SK-ickaqawask-p56-0972 <icka-+awask, face to laugh>.
senses.doubts: Includes the locative uses 'facing' (SK-ickawi--p57-0991 <icka.wi, face LOC>; SK-huuricka--p51-0862 huur+icka, image face).

senses.class: noun root (second gloss of the same noun ckaʔuʔ 'face; cloud'; plural SK-ckaraaruq-p30-0467 ckaraaruʔ 'clouds')
senses.evidence: SK-ckaraaruq-p30-0467 icka+raar+uʔ, cloud + PL + NOM; SK-ickakatakus-p57-0979 <icka+kata.kus, cloud to be sitting against (the vault of the Heavens)>; SK-ickakatasa-p57-0980 <icka-+kata.sa, cloud to be lying against (the vault of the Heavens)>.

examples.raw_etymology: <icka+kata.kus, cloud to be sitting against (the vault of the Heavens)>
<icka-+kata.sa, cloud to be lying against (the vault of the Heavens)>
<icka+raar-+kata.sa, clouds + to be lying against (the vault of the Heavens)>

senses.doubts: Parks gives 'face' and 'cloud' under one headword, so this may be one noun with two meanings rather than a homonym.

senses.class: other (no headword of its own; noun-like 'end' in ickahak, ickaʔat and descriptive 'sharp' in ickaʔu, ickaraʔuk)
senses.evidence: SK-ickaqat-p56-0971 <icka+at, go to the extremity>; SK-ickahak-p57-0975 <icka+hak, end to pass by>; SK-ickaqu-p57-0974 <icka+u, sharp + ACT>; SK-ickaraquk-p57-0981 <icka+raʔuk, make sharp>.

examples.raw_etymology: raa+icka.hak, be the end of a way

senses.doubts: I join 'end/extremity' (4 entries plus SK-uhuurickaqat-p169-3347, whose literal translation says 'image to go facing' although the word means 'be the end') and 'sharp, pointed' (3 entries) as 'the point of something'; the sources do not state that they are the same, nor whether either is the 'face' noun used figuratively. Parks does give two separate ickahak entries, 'end to pass by' (0975) and 'face to pass by' (0976).

forms.notes: 35 exact-piece etymologies (23 + 4 + 8). Initial i drops in independent words (ckaʔuʔ, ckaraaruʔ). Not counted: icka-riit in SK-ckariitkasisuq-p30-0469 (= ickariit 'hide').
